exclusions.B: whichever pupil has the turn makes a charge across the frozen lawn

WV9-P01.4.note: A pupil 'makes a charge across' a lawn: a rush or dash, i.e. a sprint; the battery context is a lure for 'energy'.

exclusions.A: it has gained a line every morning since
exclusions.B: The council's chair thanked her, but the council kept to its choice.
exclusions.C: In April the sensor went up beside the box, which stayed.
exclusions.D: In the first hard frost its battery failed, and the office's tables now show eleven blank days for Wendle Cross, the same count as Ida's one February.

WV9-P01.5.note: The author lays out ironic parallels (eleven blank days, a ruled notebook, the notice still promising an end to the walk) with dry, wry amusement; a reader could argue the irony is aimed critically at the council, so B is defensible.

exclusions.B: Tomas, who had coughed through most of the night, stacked the empty cans and said he would manage on his own.

exclusions.E: Then the radio put the next frost on Friday, and the oil truck could not come until Monday.

WV9-P03.5.note: The narrator stacks up a coming frost, no oil, no helpers and a coughing Tomas alone at the thermometer: worry; his resolve to 'manage on his own' could be read as drawing admiration, so D is defensible.
